result.name: 02_win10_semantics
keyFindings: Wrote and committed /home/iceisfun/industrial7_test_winmm/docs/research/02_win10_semantics.md (commit 8d1644c). Not pushed.

Module layout: in winmm.dll the wave/midi/mixer/aux/mmio/driver exports are 7-byte jmp stubs into winmmbase.dll. The time functions (timeGetTime, timeBeginPeriod, timeEndPeriod, timeGetDevCaps, timeGetSystemTime) live in kernel32.dll. Only PlaySound/sndPlaySound, mci*, joy*, timeSetEvent/timeKillEvent and mmsystemGetVersion (returns constant 0x30A) are implemented in winmm itself.

How winmm reaches the audio stack: the first call runs ClientUpdatePnpInfo, which waits for the AudioSrv service (polls every 2 s for up to 120 s if it is still starting), binds RPC to audiosrv, then loads the legacy drivers named in the Drivers32 entries wave/wave1..9 and midi/midi1..9 (normally wdmaud.drv). Device changes are picked up through mmdevapi's MMDeviceGetDeviceEnumerator. The wave mapper (msacm32.drv) is loaded only when the wave device count is not zero. wdmaud.drv is not in the reference corpus.

Zero devices: waveOutOpen and waveInOpen return MMSYSERR_BADDEVICEID (2) for every id, including WAVE_MAPPER and WAVE_FORMAT_QUERY, but only after parameter validation. Caps queries by id also return 2. joyGetNumDevs always returns 16.

waveOutOpen validation order: pwfx NULL -> 11; CALLBACK_WINDOW with something that is not a window -> 11; device id 0xFFFF is treated as WAVE_MAPPER; flag mask 0x7E04 for the mapper or 0x7E10 for a specific id -> 10 (so WAVE_MAPPED is invalid with the mapper, and WAVE_MAPPED_DEFAULT_COMMUNICATION_DEVICE is invalid with a specific id); phwo NULL -> 11 unless WAVE_FORMAT_QUERY; *phwo is set to NULL before the device check; then 0 devices -> 2. The callback type field is not range-checked in winmmbase, and format checks happen in the driver.

WAVEHDR checks happen before the handle check: NULL header, cbwh < 48 or an undefined flag bit (mask 0xFFFFCFE0) -> 11. Write on an unprepared header -> 34 and on a queued header -> 33. Prepare on an already-prepared header returns 0 without checking the handle. Unprepare on an unprepared header returns 0. Unprepare on a queued header returns 33. A driver answer of 8 (not supported) to prepare/unprepare counts as success.

Handle check: a handle must be above 0xFFFF, appear in the global handle list and have the expected type (1 waveOut, 2 waveIn, 3 midiOut, 4 midiIn, 5 mmio, 8 mixer, 9 midiStream), otherwise 5. A handle whose device is gone returns 6 and a handle being closed returns 12.

Caps and error text: GetDevCaps with a size of 0 returns 0 even with a NULL pointer (wave, midi, mixer, aux). waveOutGetDevCapsA copies min(size, 100) bytes. Error text: size 0 -> 0; NULL buffer -> 11; size 1 -> 0 with an empty string; valid wave codes are 0..21 and 32..35, valid midi codes 0..21 and 64..71; anything else -> 9.
DriverCallback delivers callbacks by type: 1 PostMessageA, 2 PostThreadMessageA, 3 direct function call (hdev, msg, inst, p1, p2), 5 SetEvent. A NULL target means no callback.

MIDI: midiOutOpen checks phmo first, uses flag masks 0xBFF3 (mapper) and 0x3FF3 (other ids), and does not treat 0xFFFF as the mapper. With 0 devices the mapper path returns 6. midiOutLongMsg checks the header before the handle: unprepared -> 64, queued -> 65, zero length -> 11, stream handle -> 8. midiStreamOpen requires cMidi == 1 (otherwise 11). midiStreamOut buffer length must be < 64 KiB and a multiple of 4. midiInOpen with an invalid callback window returns 7, not 11.

Mixer: mixerOpen with CALLBACK_FUNCTION -> 10. mixerGetLineInfoW checks flags first (10), then requires cbStruct >= 0x11C (284), then normalizes the output fields. mixerGetControlDetails has exact cbDetails rules (VALUE needs cbDetails >= 4, LISTTEXT needs >= 0x88).

Time: wPeriodMin is normally 1. timeGetDevCaps returns wPeriodMax = 1000000, and a bad size returns 97 (not 129). timeBeginPeriod(0) -> 97. For periods at or above the maximum timer resolution (normally 16) both timeBeginPeriod and timeEndPeriod return 0 and count nothing. Counting is per period, and an unbalanced timeEndPeriod -> 97. timeGetSystemTime with a bad size -> 129.

timeSetEvent returns 0 for invalid flags (mask 0xFFFFFE0E) and for a delay outside [wPeriodMin, 1000000]. At most 16 events can be live per process. One shared thread runs the callbacks one at a time as fptc(id, 0, dwUser, 0, 0). One-shot events free themselves after firing. timeKillEvent on an unknown or already-fired id -> 97.

mmio: mmioOpen with flags in 0xFFFC0000 returns NULL without setting wErrorRet. MMIO_PARSE, EXIST, DELETE and GETTEMP return (HMMIO)1 on success. mmioSeek with an unknown origin seeks to 0. mmioDescend with a NULL hmmio returns 258, a missing chunk returns 265, and MThd/MTrk chunk sizes are byte-swapped. mmioStringToFOURCC pads with spaces.

PlaySound: flags in mask 0xFF80DF20 -> FALSE. NULL or an empty name stops the current sound and returns TRUE. SND_NOSTOP while a sound is playing -> FALSE. ASYNC with MEMORY requires a RIFF....WAVE header and a size under 2 MiB, and the buffer is copied. A sound that is not found with SND_NODEFAULT -> FALSE.

MCI: error codes 0x200 and above carry the device id in the high word. Codes seen: 261 unrecognized command, 263 invalid device name ("new" with a verb other than open), 299 "open new" without an alias, 292 missing device name, 279 "all" not supported by the command, 300 notify on an auto-open. mciSendString(NULL) crashes because the string length is read before the NULL check (confirmed in the asm), so tests must not pass NULL.

Joystick: joyGetDevCapsW needs a size of exactly 0x2D8 or 0x308, otherwise 165. Id -1 returns 0 and fills only szRegKey. Ids of 16 or more return 6. joyGetPosEx returns 165 when the size field is below 52 or the device is not connected. joyGet/SetThreshold return 11 on error.
unknowns: None of this has been run on the Win10 VM yet; every claim comes from reading the decompiled code (plus one asm check).

wdmaud.drv is missing from the reference corpus. The following come from the driver and are marked [inference]/[VM] in the doc: the WOM_OPEN/DONE/CLOSE order, WAVEFORMATEX/EXTENSIBLE validation and WAVERR_BADFORMAT (32), what close returns while buffers are still queued, unknown CALLBACK_* types, pitch/playback-rate support, and zero-length writes.

DCB_TASK calls PostThreadMessageA(tid,msg,hDevice,dwParam1), then tail-jumps to mmTaskSignal(tid), which posts WM_USER 0x400, so the target thread gets two messages. DCB_FUNCTION calls fn(hDevice,msg,dwUser,p1,p2) and returns 1. DCB_EVENT calls SetEvent and returns 1. A NULL target or type 0, 4, 6 or 7 returns 0.

Added the mmTask semantics. mmTaskCreate(lpfn, lph, dwInst) puts an event handle in *lph (not a thread id); the event is set when lpfn returns. It returns 0, or 2 (TASKERR_OUTOFMEMORY). mmTaskBlock ignores its argument and loops on GetMessageA with no timeout until a thread message 0x400 arrives. That is a hazard: the doc's old 'round trip with bounded wait' plan was unsafe, so I replaced it. mmTaskYield is a bare ret.

Added a hazard: the first *GetNumDevs call in a process runs winmmWaitForService. It polls AudioSrv every 2 s for up to about 120 s while the service is START_PENDING, or stopped with exit code 0x435 and auto-start. Ordinal 5 is called inside winmmGetEndpointsWorker, not directly from ClientUpdatePnpInfo.

PlaySound(SND_MEMORY|SND_SYNC) returns FALSE. midiOutOpen(MIDI_MAPPER) returns MMSYSERR_ERROR (1) even though the GS synth is enumerated, because the synth needs a wave output.

Output-only device: waveInGetDevCaps(WAVE_MAPPER) succeeds ('Microsoft Sound Mapper') even with 0 waveIn devices. waveInOpen(mapper) and the waveIn format queries return 2. DRVM_MAPPER_PREFERRED_GET on waveIn returns 0 with device -1. Tests must key on GetNumDevs, not on the mapper caps.

Full caps are recorded in the doc. Device 0 is named 'Speakers (High Definition Audio' (cut to 31 chars), wMid 1, wPid 65535, formats 0xFFFFF, support 0x2E. The mapper is mid 1 / pid 2 / version 0x500. The render mix format is float32 stereo 48 kHz, and the endpoint volume is -6 dB with a range of -74 to 0 dB. Each mixer has Master Volume (DST_SPEAKERS or DST_WAVEIN) with Mute and Volume controls (0..65535, 192 steps). PCM format queries succeed for 1 or 2 channels at every rate and bit depth; 6-channel plain PCM returns WAVERR_BADFORMAT (32). DRV_QUERYFUNCTIONINSTANCEID returns the mmdevapi endpoint id. The GS Wavetable Synth is MOD_SWSYNTH with 32 voices.

Alternative cards: usb-audio uses the inbox wdma_usb/usbaudio driver and became the default render endpoint over two HDA codecs; winmm then lists the default device as id 0. ich9-intel-hda + hda-micro gives a Microphone endpoint (mixer source SRC_MICROPHONE 0x1003). AC97 and ES1370 fail with problem code 28 (no inbox driver). sb16 (ISA) is not enumerated at all. The mapper's dwSupport depends on which devices are present (0xE vs 0x2E).

Host-side playback check works: the QEMU wav audiodev records exactly what the guest renders (2 ch, 16-bit, 44.1 kHz). wavscan.py recovered the waveOut 440 and 1000 Hz tones, the PlaySound 660 Hz tone and the GS synth 880 Hz note, with correct order, frequency, level and duration, in every wav-backed boot. Gaps with no open stream are not written to the file. Capture content cannot be checked: the wav backend has no input and the none backend gives silence.

Playback protocol facts: header flags go 0x2 after prepare, 0x12 after write, 0x3 when done. TIME_SAMPLES position is exact (52920 for 1.2 s). A TIME_MS request is answered as TIME_BYTES. waveOutGetID on a mapper handle returns WAVE_MAPPER. Filling a 0.5 s capture buffer took 516-1016 ms, so timing checks must use wide bounds.
unknowns: No dedicated hda-duplex-none boot was run. It waited about 50 minutes on the shared oracle lock (35+ waiters) and I cancelled it. The audio backend is host-side only, so the guest should see the same devices as with hda-duplex-wav.
Never tried: the ISA cards adlib, gus and cs4231a, and audiodev backends other than none and wav.
The noaudio boot showed endpoints already present at the first poll, so timing for very early (pre-logon) appearance was not measured. The 120 s AudioSrv wait comes from the decomp only.
Capture content cannot be injected with the QEMU 8.2 wav or none backends, so captured data cannot be verified.

areas.d: Primary exports (must each get a real U()/UN() call): timeGetTime, timeGetSystemTime, timeGetDevCaps, timeBeginPeriod, timeEndPeriod. Timer basics, all five are winmm 7-byte jmp thunks into kernel32 (api-ms-win-mm-time-l1-1-0): timeGetTime (ord 141), timeGetSystemTime (140), timeGetDevCaps (139), timeBeginPeriod (137), timeEndPeriod (138). Verified gates [decomp kernel32 0x22840/0x1e110/0x1d190/0x6a040 + VM fc02probe]: timeGetDevCaps(NULL, sizeof) and (p, 7) -> 97 TIMERR_NOCANDO (not TIMERR_STRUCT, not INVALPARAM); (p, 8) -> 0 with wPeriodMin >= 1 (1 on the VM) and wPeriodMax == 1000000; a larger cb (e.g. 16) also 0 and bytes past 8 untouched (verify in decomp, else t_note). timeGetSystemTime(NULL,12) and (p,11) -> 129 TIMERR_STRUCT; (p,12) -> 0, wType == TIME_MS(1), u.ms within a few ms of timeGetTime(); a 16-byte MMTIME with wType preset to TIME_SAMPLES comes back TIME_MS. timeGetTime monotonic over a bounded loop (no decrease across 1000 calls, advances across Sleep(50) by >= 30 and < 2000), in step with GetTickCount (|diff| small, t_note the delta, no hard bound below ~100 ms). timeBeginPeriod/EndPeriod counting contract: Begin(0) -> 97, End(0) -> 97; Begin(1)/End(1) -> 0/0 then End(1) -> 97; nested Begin(2) x2 needs two Ends, third -> 97; unbalanced End(7) -> 97; period 15 is counted (End twice -> second 97); periods >= uMax (16 on the VM: derive uMax = ceil(NtQueryTimerResolution max/10000) at run time, never hard-code 16) such as 16, 1000, 0xFFFFFFFF are uncounted no-ops (Begin 0, End 0, End again 0). Every Begin is paired before the test returns (SAFETY). Observable effect: after Begin(1) NtQueryTimerResolution current <= 10000 (t_note; global resolution is max over processes, so only CHECK that it is not coarser than before). Also: address identity -- decode the winmm thunk (FF 25 rel32) and CHECK the IAT target equals GetProcAddress(kernel32, same name) (UIN("kernel32.dll", timeGetTime)). Threads: timeGetTime from 4 threads concurrently stays monotonic per thread. Headless, no device. Consumers: Chrome, mstscax, quartz, industrial cycle timing.

Primary exports (must each get a real U()/UN() call): timeSetEvent, timeKillEvent. timeSetEvent (ord 143) / timeKillEvent (ord 142), local winmm bodies (0x2a20/0x2e50, worker timeThread). Verified [decomp + VM pass 2]: fuEvent & 0xFFFFFE0E -> returns 0 (e.g. 2, 0x200, 0x8000); valid bits TIME_ONESHOT 0, TIME_PERIODIC 1, TIME_CALLBACK_EVENT_SET 0x10, TIME_CALLBACK_EVENT_PULSE 0x20, 0x40, 0x80, TIME_KILL_SYNCHRONOUS 0x100. uDelay 0 -> 0, uDelay 1000001 -> 0, uDelay 1000000 accepted (kill immediately); uDelay < wPeriodMin -> 0. uResolution 0 and huge values are clamped, not rejected. Return ids are nonzero, id = generation(step 0x10) + slot(id & 0xF), not reused for the next allocation. One-shot TIME_CALLBACK_FUNCTION fires exactly once with (uTimerID == returned id, uMsg == 0, dwUser == passed value, dw1 == 0, dw2 == 0) on a thread that is not the caller (GetCurrentThreadId differs; t_note the priority, TIME_CRITICAL expected, verify in decomp); killing an already-fired one-shot -> 97; killing a live periodic -> 0 and a second kill -> 97; timeKillEvent(0x12345) -> 97. NEVER use id 0 as 'unknown' (timeKillEvent(0) matches a free slot once the timer thread exists and returns 0 [VM]); a dedicated test may CHECK timeKillEvent(0) -> 97 only in a CHILD process that has never called timeSetEvent. TIME_CALLBACK_EVENT_SET: fptc is an auto/manual event HANDLE, WaitForSingleObject(ev, 2000) == WAIT_OBJECT_0; periodic EVENT_SET signals repeatedly (count >= 3 in 500 ms at 50 ms period, loose bound). TIME_CALLBACK_EVENT_PULSE on a manual-reset event: a waiter blocked before the tick wakes, the event is not left signalled afterwards. NULL function callback one-shot: returns a nonzero id, later kill -> 97 [VM]. Periodic count over 1 s at 20 ms between 25 and 75 (loose) and periodic re-arm from scheduled time (t_note drift). dwUser passes full 64-bit value. Bounded waits only (<= 2-3 s); kill every timer before returning. Consumer slice: Chrome, mstscax, quartz, dmusic, industrial apps; Industrial7 currently stubs timeSetEvent (returns 0), so these are the top-value tests.

Multi-thread and lifetime semantics of timeSetEvent/timeKillEvent (and their interaction with timeBeginPeriod). 16-slot cap per process [decomp + VM]: create 16 periodic events (long delay 10000 ms) -> all nonzero and distinct, the 17th -> 0; kill one, then a new one succeeds; ids observed differ from killed ids. Run the cap test in a CHILD process so other tests' timers do not perturb it. TIME_KILL_SYNCHRONOUS (0x100): callback sleeps 200 ms setting a flag on exit; kill from the main thread while the callback runs (signalled by an event from inside the callback) returns only after the flag is set; without 0x100 the kill may return early (t_note only). Kill from inside its own callback: timeKillEvent(own id) -> 0, no further callbacks (wait 200 ms, count unchanged), no deadlock (callback runs on the timer thread so SYNCHRONOUS must not wait on itself: verify in decomp). Callbacks are serialized on one worker thread: two periodic events record the same callback thread id and never overlap (interlocked in-callback counter max 1). timeSetEvent from several threads concurrently (4 x 4 events) returns distinct ids, then all kills -> 0. Each event holds a timeBeginPeriod(res) reference released at kill/fire: after setting and killing a 1 ms-resolution event, timeEndPeriod(1) with no own Begin -> 97 (the event's reference is gone; verify in decomp before CHECK). Callback calling timeGetTime/timeSetEvent (one-shot re-arm chain of 3) works. Process exit with a live periodic timer in a CHILD exits cleanly (exit code checked). Bounded waits, all timers killed.

Decomp, waveOutMessage/waveInMessage: anything that is not a live handle of the right type is used as a device id from its low 32 bits (waveIDMessage). Unlike waveOutGetVolume/SetVolume, these do not turn 0xFFFF into the mapper, so 0xFFFF is just an out-of-range id (2). 0x100000000 is read as id 0, and 0x1FFFFFFFF is read as the mapper.

Decomp, waveOutGetPitch/GetPlaybackRate: a NULL output gives 11 first, then the value must be a live handle, otherwise 5. There is no device-id path, so ids 0, 0xFFFF and WAVE_MAPPER all give 5 even when devices exist.

Decomp, mregHandleInternalMessages: winmmbase answers 0x801-0x804 and 0x806 itself with 8. 0x808 returns the driver's device count, 0x809 the driver's HMODULE, and 0x80A the driver's name (count = dw2-1; any failure gives 11). 0x80D/0x812 write a byte size (NULL gives 11). 0x80C copies with count = dw2/2: truncation gives 21 and count 0 gives 1. 0x811: any copy failure gives 21. 0x80E/0x80F/0x810 are the string-id queries. 0x2015 and 0x2017 work only on the mapper driver with both outputs non-NULL, otherwise 11. Every other message, including WODM_* and 0x7FFF, is passed to the driver.

The task text has two message pairs swapped. Correct values (mmddk.h, confirmed by the decomp): DRV_QUERYDEVICEINTERFACE = 0x80C, DRV_QUERYDEVICEINTERFACESIZE = 0x80D, DRV_QUERYFUNCTIONINSTANCEID = 0x811, DRV_QUERYFUNCTIONINSTANCEIDSIZE = 0x812. The tests use the correct ones.
The wave mapper is loaded when there is any waveOut or waveIn device, so expectations for the mapper depend on nout+nin, not on one direction's count.

keyFindings: Rejected calls: timeSetEvent returns 0 when fuEvent & 0xFFFFFE0E is nonzero. The accepted flag bits are exactly 0x1F1. uDelay must be between wPeriodMin and 1000000 inclusive. uResolution never causes a failure. A rejected call does not take a slot, does not advance the id generation, holds no timer period and does not change LastError. [decomp+VM]

Ids and slots: a process has 16 slots and the 17th live timer returns 0. id = 16-bit generation (advances by 0x10 on each successful allocation, skips 0) + the lowest free slot. A fresh process gets 0x10, 0x21 ... 0x10F, then 0x115 after slot 5 is killed. The generation wraps from 0xFFF0 back to 0x10. [decomp+VM, checked in child processes]

timeKillEvent requires slots[id & 0xF].id == id, otherwise it returns 97. Ids with extra high bits or another generation return 97 and leave the live timer running. Before any timeSetEvent, every id returns 97, including 0. Once slot 0 has been used and freed, timeKillEvent(0) returns 0. [VM, child processes only]

Timer period: period = TimerData (16) if uResolution > TimerData, else max(uResolution, wPeriodMin); if uDelay < period, TimerData is used. The timer holds one timeBeginPeriod reference until it is killed or a one-shot finishes. The tests observe this through timeEndPeriod returning 0 or 97, and every probe is balanced. A full-table failure gives its reference back. [decomp+VM]

Callbacks: the function is called as fptc(id, 0, dwUser, 0, 0), and dwUser keeps its full 64-bit value. All callbacks run one at a time on a single shared timer thread at THREAD_PRIORITY_TIME_CRITICAL (15). That thread is created lazily by the first timeSetEvent and waits alertably, so a queued APC runs on it. [decomp+VM]

Callback type is fuEvent & 0xF0: 0 calls the function, 0x10 calls SetEvent, 0x20 calls PulseEvent. Any other value (0x30, 0x40, 0x80, ...) is accepted but nothing is dispatched; a one-shot still finishes and later kills return 97. [decomp+VM]

Inside a callback, timeKillEvent on its own one-shot returns 0, and the period is released only once. A timer can kill itself with TIME_KILL_SYNCHRONOUS without deadlocking. timeSetEvent can be chained from a callback. With TIME_KILL_SYNCHRONOUS, a kill from another thread waits for that timer's running callback; without the flag it returns at once. [decomp+VM]

Periodic timers are scheduled from the arm time plus k * uDelay, so they do not drift: tick 25 at 20 ms landed at 500-501 ms. Missed ticks after a stall are dispatched back to back (35 callbacks in 700 ms despite a 400 ms stall). [decomp+VM, loose bounds]
